when: Compares group means on a continuous outcome while controlling for one or more continuous covariates.
example: Two teaching methods are compared on final exam scores, but students began with different prior grades. ANCOVA compares the methods on the final score after fairly adjusting for those starting grades.
small_sample: A well-chosen covariate can recover power in a small study by reducing error variance. Confirm the covariate was measured before treatment and that the slopes are parallel across groups.
assumptions: The covariate is measured before the treatment and is unaffected by it
The covariate relates linearly to the outcome
Regression slopes are homogeneous across groups
Residuals are roughly normal with similar variances
alternative: One-way ANOVA on the raw outcome, when no covariate is justified

# survey_skeleton.R
# StatChooser sample survey skeleton (surveyframe method = "ancova").
# Section A is a standard demographic block. Section B, and C/D/E where present,
# carry the measures the analysis plan needs. Replace every [bracketed] stem
# with your own validated items before fielding the survey.
# install.packages("surveyframe")
library(surveyframe)

# ---- Choice sets (define once, reuse) ----
agree5 <- sf_choices("agree5", 1:5,
  c("Strongly disagree", "Disagree", "Neutral", "Agree", "Strongly agree"))
grp_set <- sf_choices("grp_set", 1:3, c("Group 1", "Group 2", "Group 3"))
gender_cs <- sf_choices("gender_cs",
  c("woman", "man", "nonbinary", "selfdescribe", "na"),
  c("Woman", "Man", "Non-binary", "Prefer to self-describe", "Prefer not to say"))
edu_cs <- sf_choices("edu_cs", 1:5,
  c("Secondary or below", "Diploma", "Bachelor degree", "Master degree", "Doctorate"))
role_cs <- sf_choices("role_cs", 1:4,
  c("Entry or junior", "Mid-level", "Senior or manager", "Executive or owner"))
industry_cs <- sf_choices("industry_cs", 1:5,
  c("Manufacturing", "Retail or trade", "Services", "Public sector", "Other"))

# ---- Section A: Respondent profile ----
sec_a <- sf_item("sec_a", "Section A: Respondent profile", type = "section_break",
  section_intro = "A few background questions about you.")
age <- sf_item("age", "Your age in years", type = "numeric")
gender <- sf_item("gender", "Your gender", type = "single_choice", choice_set = "gender_cs")
education <- sf_item("education", "Highest level of education completed", type = "single_choice", choice_set = "edu_cs")
job_role <- sf_item("job_role", "Your role or seniority", type = "single_choice", choice_set = "role_cs")
experience <- sf_item("experience", "Years of experience", type = "numeric")
industry <- sf_item("industry", "Your industry or sector", type = "single_choice", choice_set = "industry_cs")

# ---- Section B: Group, covariate, and outcome ----
sec_b <- sf_item("sec_b", "Section B: Group, covariate, and outcome", type = "section_break")
group_var <- sf_item("group_var", "[group membership - replace]", type = "single_choice", choice_set = "grp_set")
covariate_var_1 <- sf_item("covariate_var_1", "[Covariate 1 item 1 - replace stem]", type = "likert", choice_set = "agree5", scale_id = "covariate_var")
covariate_var_2 <- sf_item("covariate_var_2", "[Covariate 1 item 2 - replace stem]", type = "likert", choice_set = "agree5", scale_id = "covariate_var")
covariate_var_3 <- sf_item("covariate_var_3", "[Covariate 1 item 3 - replace stem]", type = "likert", choice_set = "agree5", scale_id = "covariate_var")
covariate_var <- sf_scale("covariate_var", "Covariate 1", c("covariate_var_1", "covariate_var_2", "covariate_var_3"), method = "mean")
outcome_var_1 <- sf_item("outcome_var_1", "[Outcome item 1 - replace stem]", type = "likert", choice_set = "agree5", scale_id = "outcome_var")
outcome_var_2 <- sf_item("outcome_var_2", "[Outcome item 2 - replace stem]", type = "likert", choice_set = "agree5", scale_id = "outcome_var")
outcome_var_3 <- sf_item("outcome_var_3", "[Outcome item 3 - replace stem]", type = "likert", choice_set = "agree5", scale_id = "outcome_var")
outcome_var <- sf_scale("outcome_var", "Outcome", c("outcome_var_1", "outcome_var_2", "outcome_var_3"), method = "mean")

# ---- Analysis plan (ids match the items and scales above) ----
plan_entry <- list(
  id                = "RQ1",
  research_question = "Do the groups differ in the outcome after controlling for the covariate?",
  family            = "group_comparison",
  method            = "ancova",
  roles             = list(
    group      = "group_var",
    covariates = c("covariate_var"),
    outcome    = "outcome_var"
  ),
  options           = list(alpha = 0.05)
)

# ---- Assemble the instrument ----
instr <- sf_instrument(
  title         = "[Your study title]",
  description   = "[Population and purpose]",
  components    = list(
    sec_a, age, gender, education, job_role, experience, industry, sec_b, group_var, covariate_var_1, covariate_var_2, covariate_var_3, covariate_var, outcome_var_1, outcome_var_2, outcome_var_3, outcome_var
  ),
  analysis_plan = list(plan_entry)
)
